units.title: Counting Numbers: 1-10

outcomes.text: Count by 1s (forwards and backwards) to 10
Represent the number of objects in a group with a written numeral 0 to 10.
Count to answer “how many” questions (up to 5); Given a number to 5, count out how many objects
Identify, compare and order groups of 1 to 5 objects
Demonstrate an understanding of the relative size of numbers1 to 5, quickly naming a number that is 1 more or less than a number to 5, and solve related word problems (orally)
Demonstrate fluency with addition and subtraction by quickly naming a number that is 1 more or less than a number to 5
Demonstrate an understanding of repeating patterns by duplicating and extending element sound or action pattern

resources: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

units.title: Counting How Many: 1-10

outcomes.text: Count on or backwards from any number between 1 and 10
Count to answer “how many” questions (up to 10); Given a number to 10, count out how many objects
Partition or decompose 5 objects into 2 parts to identify combinations to 5 and record the partition symbolically
Identify, compare and order groups of 1 to 10 objects
Demonstrate addition/subtracting by acting out an ‘+’ or ‘–‘ word problem sums to 5, using putting together and counting all or taking away part and counting the rest.
Duplicate and extend 3 element sound or action pattern

resources: Empty containers in the classroom corner shop/market

mental.title: Play “How Many Fingers Up” (using one hand)
mental.title_nl: Sange“Kitti dorommu manime na Kammun di’’ (ti kittin baane)

steps.text: Holding some fingers up with one hand. Have pupils call out the number of fingers they see up.
N kittin dorommu manime na KAMMUN DI? A koyi an ga da kittin dorommu beenu wari kammun di walla xa ti nomban kayiti ŋa.
Do this with other numbers of fingers up.

mental.title: Play “One more (or less) than”.
mental.title_nl: Sange “ Baane kamma ( ma a wure)”

steps.text: Call out a number from 1 to 5. Have pupils call out a number that is 1 more (or less) than the number given (or a card picked).
O wa riini sanga; n wa riini nomban ko, xa na nomba ko ke be ga 1 kamma ti nomba be ga koni.
Do this with different numbers (1 to 5).
Repeat the activity with 1 less than the number called.
O wa riini saage sange ke ya; ƞa nomban kayitinun koyini xa ya, xa na nomba kon’in da ke be ga 1 wure ti nomban kayiti ƞa.
Do this with different numbers (1 to 5).

mental.title: Play “Show me ___” numbers 1 to 5 with fingers
mental.title_nl: Sange“ Nombanun koy’in ƞa ____” na a wuttu 1 katta 5 ti kittin dorommu ƞa.

steps.text: Call out a number. Pupils show that many fingers in the air. Then have pupils play game in pairs.
O wa riini sanga; N wa nomba konno, xa n’a ko n'a koyikoy’in ƞa kittin dorommu manime na hanken di.
Have pupils play the game in pairs. One calls out number, the other shows fingers; then both write the number in their jotter.

reinforcement.title: Play “What number is larger (or smaller)?” with numbers 1 to 5
reinforcement.title_nl: Sange “ Kan jaate gabe ni ( ma ho roxe)? Jaatun 1 katta 5

- 7 na 6 do 8 ya naxa;

objectives: do Subtraction by comparing to find “how many more”

activities.title: Subtraction: Comparing to Find “How Many More”?
activities.title_nl: Bogumande: Xensende na “Gabe Tan’a muuru”

steps.text: Present pupils with problems involving comparing, E.g.,
1. Xalibu 9 ñi Awa maxa. 6 wa Buba maxa. Gaben n’a ko maxa? Manime tana?
2. Xalibu 3 tana wa Awa maxa nan hunu Buba ya. Gelli xalibu 7 ga n’a ñi Awa maxa, xalibu manime na Buba maxa?
Write corresponding subtraction statement on board (i.e., 8 − 6 = __); 5 − 3 = __) so and help pupils see the connection between the situation and the statement and find the answer.
Give pupils more examples to solve, and for each,
Bogumanden digaamun saha an walahan di, a timmandi ti kontindi hoonu ¿a ti xensenden ¿a do an na a ko an ga da a jaabi moxo be ya.
Have pupils do G1PB Activity 1.9.2.

closure.assessment: Have learners listen and solve the word problems: a. Haja had 7 pencils. Musa has 5. Ho has more? How many more? b. Amie has 3 more pencils than Musa. If Amie has 8 pencils, how many pencils does Musa have?
closure.homework: Ask learners to create a problem that involves comparison of two numbers to find which has more and how many more.

lessons.title: Subtraction: Take Away From, and Finding What is Left
lessons.objectives_intro: By the end of the lesson the learner should be able to:
objectives: Do Subtraction by Take-Away From, and Finding What is Left

activities.title: Subtraction: Taking Away From, and Finding What is Left
activities.title_nl: Nan Wutundi Bakka ho Di, do na a Muuru Manin Toxo

steps.text: Present pupils with subtraction problems involving taking away from, E.g.,
1. “Kontindi hoonu 9 ñi Awa taabalin kamma. Gelli Buba ga na a kontindi hoonu 2 wutu, manimen toxo a taabalin kamma?”
2. Leemunu 8 wa Buba maxa. 3 wa Awa maxa. Gelli Buba ga na 2 kini Awa ya, manimen toxo sere baane su maxa?
Write corresponding subtraction statements on board (i.e., 9 – 2 = __; 8 − 1 = __) and help pupils see the connection between the situation and the statement and find the answer.
Give pupils more examples to solve, and for each,
Bogumanden digaamun saha an walahan di, a timmandi ti kontindi hoonun ¿a ti nan wutundi bakka ho di do an na a ko an ga da a jaabi moxo be ya. Have pupils do G1PB Activity 1.9.3.

closure.assessment: Write the subtraction statements below for learners to solve and explain the strategy you used. 17 - ___= 15 15 - ___= 14 14 - ___= 11
closure.homework: Have learners copy and complete the subtraction statements as homework. 14 - ___= 12 18 - ___= 17

steps.text: Display cutout shapes with different colours on the table. Put the class into groups to play the game.
Leminan baane na bogu sappa baane di a na kayitin sagara tagemoxon do koola ya, a na tagemoxonu muuru do na i konti kubeenu gan baana ti koola be ga sagare.
